messages.author: bbe66d40f38994b4
messages.subject: Evaluating spatially explicit density estimates of unmarked wildlife detected by remote cameras: Evans, Michael J., & Rittenhouse, Tracy A. G. (2019)
parts:
It might be odd to ask for help about something that is not directly related to the "unmarked" package. 
I am replicating the analysis for Evans, Michael J., & Rittenhouse, Tracy A. G. (2019). Evaluating spatially explicit density estimates of unmarked wildlife detected by remote cameras, using the given R code and Data. I am confused how to interpret a model results. For example the null model produces the following results;

                              initial values = 1005.753 0.5521531 0.6296791 423 

                                  iter 100 21:06:54 
                         current = 970.0077 0.7688064 0.4745503 271 -784.7343 
                            Acceptance rates
                                    S = 0.8966667 
                                      w = 0.7666667
What does initial values mean and how to interpret these?
How to interpret values of S and w?

Note: I am posting it here after getting no response from the corresponding author of the paper. Any help will be highly appreciated .

Data (as an R-list) and the code provided by the author, are attached here.

messages.author: 4a635fe980c8c1cd
messages.subject: Re: Evaluating spatially explicit density estimates of unmarked wildlife detected by remote cameras: Evans, Michael J., & Rittenhouse, Tracy A. G. (2019)
parts:
This might be a better general resource for this sort of analysis (https://groups.google.com/forum/#!forum/spatialcapturerecapture).

As a very quick/cursory answer, the initial values reflect where the model has started the MCMC simulation. I think--based on a quick read of the code that may or may not be correct--that from right to left, the current values should be the negative log-likelihood, abundance, the expected proportion of augmented individuals that exist, lam0, and sigma. The acceptance rates, I suppose, relate to the proposed proportion of MCMC iterations in which the proposed values for S (I guess estimates of the activity center locations) and w (the number of augmented individuals estimated to actually exist in the defined state space) have been accepted. As best I can tell very quickly, the first function--and the function I think you have used?--is the same algorithm presented by Chandler and Royle (2013). I think the initial paper (Chandler and Royle) might be a good place to find more in depth information, or chapter...15(? 16?) in the Spatial Capture-Recapture book, if you have access to it.  But as a starting point, these aren't results yet--more like an update on where the model is currently sampling and how the algorithm has performed so far.



John
